why: What a cut's picture is checked for before it is picked (studio2/checks.py): each row is one question a reader answers from the picture, built from the cut as planned. A row is a floor (a failed try cannot be picked) only where calibration bore it out: kept stage-1 pictures pass it, rejected and crossed ones fail it, on every run (calibration below, measured by studio2 checks calibrate). Every other row is advice the deciding agent reads. A new check is a row.

opens_shown.asks: Is the thing shown {opens_means}, as described: {what}?

part_shown.asks: Is {part} clearly visible in the picture?

count_right.asks: How many {part} are there in the picture? (count them)

flow_room.asks: Is the way {flow} visible and uncluttered, so a line drawn along it would read?

text_free.asks: Is the picture free of any letters, numbers, words, logos or watermarks?

anatomy_ok.asks: Are the people and things in it whole and correctly formed (no extra or missing limbs, nothing melted, merged or impossible)?

same_place.asks: Is it the same place as the reference picture (the last image) - the same kind of room, walls, floor, equipment and look - seen anew?

edit_only_change.asks: Compared with the original (the last image), is this picture the same composition, camera and objects, with only this changed: {change}?

change_shown.asks: Compared with the original (the last image), can you see this change: {change}?

change_read.asks: (a blind viewer, shown the picked first and this last picture with nothing else, says what changed; v1's matcher compares it with the cut's change)
